Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot. We’re seeing correlated error rates and token-latency spikes in the US-west streaming cluster starting at 07:58 PDT. I’ve opened a support ticket (SUP-4982) and looped the on-call infra and SRE.

Immediate actions we recommend while we triage:
- Short-term client-side workarounds (apply now):
  * Enable polling fallback for 30s windows: if streaming chunks do not arrive for >1.5s, fall back to conflated poll for the next 20–30s.
  * Reduce max_tokens per call by 20% to shorten in-flight generation windows.
  * Disable client-side optimistic auto-retry: let Redwood take the adaptive retry to avoid duplicate inflight load.
- Our side: we are triggering a constrained-routing failover for affected session routes to a lower-latency shard and scaling the streaming pool.

I’ll share a short status note in 30 minutes with what we find.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Escalations Lead, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: [URGENT] live chat sessions stuttering (started 08:00 PDT)

Quick technical summary and action items from runtime:

Findings so far:
- A control-plane rollout for a new kernel selection policy started at 07:54 PDT and caused higher-than-expected queueing for streaming KV cache priming on certain edges (us-west-2).
- The affected workload pattern shows many short-turn conversations (avg seq len 80 tokens) that suffer when the kernel switch results in reduced batching efficiency.

Immediate mitigations applied by Redwood (done 08:40 PDT):
1) Rolled back kernel-policy to previous stable version for the us-west streaming pool.
2) Forced route failover for 3% of sessions on the most impacted hosts to an un-rolled pool (fallback path).
3) Temporarily increased the streaming pool autoscaling headroom and disabled speculative kernel updates.

Suggested customer-side configs we recommend for next 24 hours:
- Use the SDK param streaming_buffer_ms: 300 (default 100) to smooth chunk reassembly and reduce perceived stutter.
- Add client-side jitter tolerance: only treat response as failed after 3 consecutive missed chunk heartbeats.
- If your latency SLO allows, enable the ‘compact-stream’ mode (reduces per-token overhead but may mix partial outputs).

We’ve attached a short set of commands you can run if you want us to test a session from your environment (see drive link). We’ll keep the rollback in place until midnight PDT and monitor for recurrence.

Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Sarah / Redstone team —

We’ve kept monitoring overnight and the rollback/staging failover removed the large majority of the token pacing spikes. From 03:00–06:00 PDT the error/latency curves returned to baseline.

Next steps we propose (short post-incident plan):
1) Postmortem: Redwood will share an incident timeline, root cause analysis, and remediation plan by 2028-05-18 EOD. We’ll include telemetry and proof of the rollback effectiveness.
2) Targeted mitigations for customers: we’ll publish a short client-runbook with the SDK flags above and a reversible config template to apply for ~48 hours in similar situations.
3) SLA exception: because this incident impacted peak sessions, we are prepared to propose a one-time credit for May usage; I’ll loop Finance and your account rep if you’d like to discuss.
4) Preventive work: we will gate kernel-policy rollouts behind canary tests that simulate high short-turn conversational workloads; ETA for the change: 3 weeks.

If Redstone would like us to run a joint test against your staging traffic, we can schedule a 30-minute window tomorrow. What time works best for you?

Thanks for the patience and for the helpful telemetry — it sped up diagnosis.

Best,
Ben Carter
